result:
Both concerns were correct, and re-reading your note before handoff caught two more sections that had been added since my first read — those are closed too.

**Concern 1 — compiler identity.** You're right and my v4 text was wrong. `NativeContextV2.toolchain` carries `rustcVersion`/`rustCommitHash`; the TypeScript context carries `compilerName`/`compilerVersion`/`compilerPackageDigest`; both are reachable through the universe's own `nativeContextId`, which `close_run` already requires to be Plan-selected. Stronger than I credited: `admit_native_context` already refuses `native-context-compiler-version-not-from-manifest` for both languages, so binding here inherits a chain from a retained closure manifest. My "Rust carries no rustc toolchain identity" sentence is withdrawn, and `languageMode`+`synthesizerVersion` (option synthesis, not the language) with it.

**Concern 2 — representability.** Reproduced your exact number as a check: 21 entries, 723 bytes, u8 max 255. `languageVersion` is now the raw 32 bytes of `SHA-256(C(body-language-version))` — the same fixed-width treatment the inherited grammar gives `levelVersion`, retention `derived`, inherited frame grammar unchanged.

**Mixed-edition ownership**, per your decision: new `native.source-unit-ownership.v1` with `{path, unitId, crateName, targetEdition}` rows and a required-nullable `sourceUnitOwnershipId`. Exact path equality, agreeing owners admissible, every other outcome refusing with its own cause. Bodies at 2021 and 2015 both commit in one universe.

**Your two later sections:**
- *Target edition* — you found a real soundness bug: `if len(distinct)==1` skipped ownership whenever package defaults agreed. Gone. No fast path at all; `targetEdition: null` defers to the package map so the two committed places cannot contradict. The same-package two-target/two-edition control is in the suite; both commit with different identities.
- *Body vs provider language* — also a live defect: a `.js` body could not carry the `javascript` identifier §6.3 requires. `languageId` is now derived from the source variant, frame and record from one derivation over one anchor, and the frame's language must be one the engine's binding declares. A real JS clone Run through the TypeScript engine commits; a byte-identical `.ts` body has a different identity. `cross-tsjs` untouched.

Checks: identity **559/559**, foundation 231/231, array-orders 65/65, product-config 28/28, product-quality 24/24, workflows 1290/1290, native **151/151** and security 456/456 (out of tree, so I did not repeat the v4 report-overwrite — the generated report is byte-identical to the frozen image).

Three things to flag plainly:

1. **`check-integration.py` fails in tree** — the stale copied builder writes no `sourceUnitOwnershipId`. I did not edit your file; I verified out of tree that adding `'sourceUnitOwnershipId':None` at `integration-fixtures.py:199` restores 363/363. I chose required-and-nullable over optional deliberately (the `preparedOutputSetId` precedent), and that one line is the cost.
2. **Every TypeScript and Rust `bodyIdentity` value changed** from my first v5 draft; any vector you cached is stale. Ownership rows now have four fields, not three.
3. One negative — an empty edition map — is **not measurable by Run-level neutralisation**, and I'm reporting that rather than a status I didn't establish: any permissive fallback must invent a dialect that never matches an already-minted frame. It's measured at the function boundary instead, where a guessing implementation is shown silently choosing 2015. Three probe runs were superseded by my own source changes and are retained with truthful in-file labels.

Handoff at `/tmp/opensip-design-corrections/digest-corrections-author.v5/`. No acceptance or readiness claim, and I don't claim all gaps are closed — corrected v9 freeze, fresh review at zero unresolved MUST/SHOULD, new blind, and full application review all remain required.
